content.user_title: Migrate Logseq Graphs to DB Format
content.value_statement: Moving Logseq Markdown graphs to DB format can break tags, properties, references, and queries. This skill guides planning, import choices, validation, and fixes.
actual_capabilities: Explains when and why to migrate a Logseq Markdown graph to DB format.
Provides a pre-migration checklist for backups, pages, properties, tags, and namespaces.
Compares migration options for tags, namespaces, property typing, and import strategy.
Suggests post-migration validation checks for pages, blocks, properties, and queries.
Documents common migration issues and practical recovery steps.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not perform the migration automatically.
It depends on Logseq DB behavior, which the source describes as alpha.
It cannot guarantee that every graph, plugin, query, or whiteboard will migrate correctly.
It does not replace a verified backup and manual review of imported data.

use_cases.title: Plan a Personal Graph Migration
use_cases.description: A Logseq user prepares a graph for DB import and needs decisions for tags, properties, namespaces, and backups.

use_cases.title: Validate Imported Knowledge Bases
use_cases.description: A researcher checks whether pages, references, properties, and queries still work after moving to DB format.

use_cases.title: Support Team Migration Reviews
use_cases.description: A team lead compares migration strategies before changing shared workflows, sync expectations, and class structures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Migration Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning before any import work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare my Logseq Markdown graph for DB migration. Create a checklist for backups, tags, properties, namespaces, and queries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Import Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup before importing exported data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Logseq migration choices. Help me decide how to handle tags, namespaces, property types, and page references during DB import.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Migration Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: My Logseq DB migration changed some links, tags, and property values. Help me identify likely causes and create a repair plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Validation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for important or large graphs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a post-migration validation plan for a large Logseq graph. Include page counts, orphaned blocks, property checks, query updates, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: I have a small personal Logseq graph and want to move from Markdown to DB format.
output: Recommended approach: migrate the whole graph after creating a verified backup.
Main checks: review tags, property formats, namespaces, and critical pages before import.
After import: compare page counts, inspect important links, and keep the Markdown graph unchanged.

output_examples.input: My migrated graph has broken references and old queries do not work.
output: Likely causes: renamed pages, namespace changes, and DB attribute differences.
Repair path: identify broken links, update old query attributes, and review affected namespaces.
Validation step: test important pages before treating the DB graph as the primary copy.

output_examples.input: Our team wants to migrate a large shared graph without disrupting daily work.
output: Recommended approach: run Markdown and DB graphs in parallel during evaluation.
Team decisions: define class rules, property types, sync expectations, and rollback criteria.
Review cadence: test key workflows before moving active work to the DB graph.

best_practices: Create and verify a complete backup before importing any graph into DB format.
Test migration with a small subset before changing a large or active graph.
Compare pages, blocks, properties, links, and queries before using the DB graph as primary.
anti_patterns: Deleting the Markdown graph immediately after a successful import screen.
Assuming every tag should become a class without reviewing its purpose.
Migrating a team graph without documenting sync, plugin, and query differences.

faq.question: Does this skill migrate my graph automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, validation, and troubleshooting guidance for a Logseq migration.

faq.question: Should I delete my Markdown graph after import?
faq.answer: No. Keep the Markdown graph as a backup until the DB graph is fully verified.

faq.question: Can it help with broken page references?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains likely causes and suggests checks for renamed pages and namespace changes.

faq.question: Does it cover property type changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains typed properties and common cases where values migrate as text.

faq.question: Is Logseq DB treated as stable?
faq.answer: No. The source notes alpha status and recommends careful backups and validation.

faq.question: Can teams use this for shared graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports strategy review, parallel operation, workflow updates, and validation planning.
